panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Frontal clinical photograph of the patient at rest showing markedly reduced facial expression; the caption explicitly labels this panel 'Hypomimia (A)' and the text states hypomimia was reported in the clinical records and remains evident in Fig. 1, a recognized facial manifestation of urofacial syndrome. Hypomimia itself is absent from the finding vocabulary, so it is recorded as a proposed finding. B: Clinical photograph of the same patient attempting to smile, with the mouth corners pulling into a crying/sad expression - the classic inverted (Ochoa) smile that is the hallmark facial sign of urofacial syndrome, directly supported by the panel caption.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: Clinical photograph of the index urofacial syndrome patient's face at rest, part of the compound Figure 1a,b that the text cites as demonstrating her inverted facial expression. No smile is attempted in this panel, so it serves as the baseline/comparison view rather than showing the hallmark sign directly, hence lower confidence and no typicality rating. b: Clinical photograph of the patient's attempted smile showing the paradoxical/inverted (Ochoa) facial expression, the hallmark sign of urofacial syndrome and the explicit subject of the article title and caption. Real human patient with eyes de-identified; no third-party copyright noted.
